{
  "research_question": "How do five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance metrics including Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": [
    "Combined",
    "ICMS Only",
    "Dim Visual Only",
    "Bright Visual Only",
    "Sham"
  ],
  "response_variables": [
    "Time-to-Target",
    "Success",
    "Path Efficiency",
    "Average Speed",
    "AD"
  ],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct a separate one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) for each of the five response variables to test the null hypothesis that the mean performance metric is equal across all five stimulation paradigms.",
    "Model specification: Y_ijk = mu + tau_i + epsilon_ijk, where Y is the response variable, mu is the grand mean, tau_i is the effect of the i-th stimulation paradigm, and epsilon_ijk is the random error term.",
    "Test statistic: F = MS_between / MS_within, comparing the variance between paradigm means to the variance within paradigms."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If any ANOVA yields a statistically significant F-statistic (p < 0.05), proceed to pairwise comparisons between all five stimulation paradigms.",
    "Calculate pairwise differences in mean performance for each response variable.",
    "Compute 95% Confidence Intervals for the mean differences to quantify the magnitude and direction of effects."
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Apply the Bonferroni correction to the family-wise error rate. Since there are 5 response variables and up to 10 pairwise comparisons per variable (5 choose 2), the adjusted significance threshold will be alpha_adj = 0.05 / (5 * 10) = 0.001 for individual tests, or alternatively, apply the correction strictly within each variable's set of 10 comparisons (alpha_adj = 0.05 / 10 = 0.005).",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Do not use Ordinary Linear Regression as the response variables are continuous but the predictor (Stim Paradigm) is categorical with 5 unordered levels, making a linear trend assumption inappropriate. Instead, recommend a Generalized Linear Model (GLM) framework. For continuous outcomes (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD), use a One-Way ANOVA (which is equivalent to GLM with Gaussian identity link) or a Linear Mixed Effects Model if 'Mouse' is treated as a random effect to account for repeated measures. For the binary outcome 'Success', explicitly recommend a Binomial GLM (Logistic Regression) with Stim Paradigm as a fixed effect.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality: Residuals for each ANOVA must be approximately normally distributed; check via Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests.",
    "Homogeneity of Variance: Variances across the five paradigms must be equal for each response variable; check via Levene's test or Bartlett's test.",
    "Independence: Observations must be independent; verify that data points from the same mouse do not violate independence assumptions (may require mixed-effects modeling if violations occur).",
    "Outliers: Inspect extreme values in Time-to-Target (max 201.39) and Path Efficiency (max 29.82) to ensure they do not unduly influence the F-statistic."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "The 'Combined' paradigm likely shows superior performance (lower Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency, higher Average Speed, lower AD) compared to the 'Sham' control, indicating a synergistic effect of stimulation.",
    "Sensory deprivation paradigms ('Dim Visual Only', 'Bright Visual Only') may show intermediate or degraded performance compared to 'Combined' but potentially better than 'ICMS Only' depending on the reliance of the task on visual cues.",
    "Significant differences are expected in 'Success' rates and 'Time-to-Target' given the binary nature of success and the continuous nature of time, likely driven by the large sample size (n=76655).",
    "'Path Efficiency' and 'AD' are expected to differ significantly, reflecting changes in navigation strategy and spatial precision across paradigms."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The dataset summary indicates potential imbalance in sample sizes across paradigms (Combined: 48846 vs Sham: 3505), which could bias ANOVA results if variances are unequal (heteroscedasticity).",
    "The variable 'Path Efficiency' has a very wide range (0.0009 to 29.82) and high standard deviation relative to the mean, suggesting a potentially skewed distribution that may violate normality assumptions.",
    "The 'Success' variable is binary (0/1), rendering standard ANOVA inappropriate without transformation or the use of specific GLMs as recommended.",
    "Potential confounding by 'Mouse' ID (8 levels) is not explicitly controlled in a simple one-way ANOVA, risking pseudoreplication if multiple trials per mouse are aggregated without accounting for subject variability."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a Linear Mixed Effects Model for the continuous variables and a Generalized Linear Mixed Model (GLMM) with a binomial link for 'Success', including 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for within-subject correlation and to handle the unbalanced design more robustly than one-way ANOVA."
}
